gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured heat, power or bitrate figure for the picks: DashCamTalk tester Augustus logged the 70mai A810S at 82.4 °C at the microSD slot after about 30 minutes parked in sun (28.1 °C outside) without a shutdown and at 29.4 Mb/s front against 10.1 Mb/s rear, and Panzer Platform measured the VIOFO A229 Plus at 6.16 W recording and 5.71 W in low-bitrate parking in its 3-channel form.
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages dashcamtalk.com/best-dash-cams, the PCWorld roundup and knowledgelib.io, plus productbible.com. None gives a measured bitrate, wattage or surface temperature for any candidate; PCWorld has only a generic parked draw of 0.25 to 0.45 A, and knowledgelib and DashCamTalk's roundup already carry the A810 Lite's 24/25 fps two-channel cap, so that one finding is not new. Vortex Radar (cited) returned HTTP 403 and thecargearguide.com failed on a certificate error, so neither was read. Limits: the figures are from named DashCamTalk forum testers, not a lab; they are not on one common metric across candidates; the A229 Plus power figures are 3-channel on 2023 firmware; and there is no measurement at all for our DDPAI N5 Pro.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's order and does not change it. The A810S rear channel records at about a third of the front's data rate (10.1 against 29.4 Mb/s, 1080p), which backs putting the A229 Plus first when the rear view matters; Chuck McCoy reports the A229 Plus keeps its bitrate with two or three cameras running, but no Mbps figure for it appeared in page text. The A810 Lite's front camera falls to 24 fps with the rear connected, which weakens it as the budget pick. The heat figures give hot-climate shoppers a number (A810S card slot 82.4 °C, no shutdown). Nothing measured supports or undermines our DDPAI N5 Pro row, so it has to stand on maker specs (2K rear, built-in 64 GB eMMC).

findings.label: Power draw while recording, 3-channel (front 1440p + rear 1440p + cabin 1080p)
findings.source_title: A229 Plus Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Measured by DashCamTalk tester Panzer Platform on firmware V1.0 0922, quoted in triops44's post of 2023-11-07. This is the 3-channel setup, not the 2-channel front + rear kit ChatGPT showed, so the 2CH kit should draw less. The tester warns the figures may change with firmware.

findings.label: Power draw in low-bitrate parking mode, 3-channel
findings.source_title: A229 Plus Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Panzer Platform's figure; Chuck McCoy (2023-11-16) restates it as the 3-CH low-bitrate figure and works out 74 Wh ÷ 5.71 W = 12.9 hours on a 20,000 mAh power bank. Our arithmetic: 0.453 A × 24 h = 10.9 Ah a day from the car battery; parking mode needs VIOFO's hardwire kit, sold separately.

findings.label: Power and heat against the 4K A229 Pro, 3-channel
findings.value: 1.79 W less while recording (6.16 W against 7.95 W); runs 28 °F (16 °C) cooler
findings.source_title: A229 Plus Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Panzer Platform, quoted by triops44 on 2023-11-07. The page does not state ambient temperature or where on the body the temperature was taken. The A229 Pro 2CH is over this page's budget.

findings.label: Bitrate when more cameras are connected
findings.value: No reduction in 2-channel or 3-channel use; the A229 Pro's front drops from 57 Mbps to about 35 Mbps in 3-channel
findings.source_title: A229 Plus Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Chuck McCoy, 2023-11-09. The post gives no Mbps number for the A229 Plus itself.

findings.label: Parking-mode saving with GPS off, 1-channel
findings.value: 0.12 to 0.14 W less (10 to 11 mA at 12.6 V); about 100 minutes more projected parking time
findings.source_title: VIOFO A229 Plus - Testing / Review - RCG (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: rcg530, 2024-03-04, firmware v1.2_240227. rcg530's per-mode wattage tables for 1CH, 2CH and 3CH are posted as images that I could not read.

findings.label: Recorded bitrate, front + rear recording together
findings.value: Front 29.4 Mb/s (2160p HEVC, 30 fps, HDR); rear 10.1 Mb/s (1080p HEVC, 30 fps, HDR)
findings.note: Augustus, post of 2026-04-03 (edited 2026-05-31). LateralNW gives the same 29.4 Mb/s front figure on 2026-01-13 (https://dashcamtalk.com/forum/threads/70mai-a810s-4k-review-ln.60320/post-665405). The rear channel gets about a third of the front's data rate.

findings.label: File data rate per channel, normal recording (second tester)
findings.value: Front 3.66 MB/s, rear 1.22 MB/s, front sub-stream 0.26 MB/s; 5.14 MB/s total
findings.note: rcg530, 2026-04-13. Our arithmetic: × 8 gives about 29.3 Mbps front and 9.8 Mbps rear, matching Augustus; 5.14 MB/s is about 18.5 GB an hour. rcg530's power test (2025-12-20, firmware v1.1.26ww, UP03 hardwire kit) is posted as images I could not read.

findings.label: Surface temperature after about 30 minutes parked facing the sun, recording 4K 30 fps two-channel
findings.value: microSD slot 82.4 °C, LCD 70.1 °C, top 64.5 °C, underside 60.1 °C; did not shut down
findings.note: Augustus, 2026-04-03, firmware 1.5.40ww, stock power supply. Outside 28.1 °C, cabin 32.7 °C, dashboard 53.5 °C. One test on one unit; the hottest point is where the memory card sits.

findings.label: Wi-Fi file transfer speed to phone
findings.value: 3.66 MB/s (a one-minute 4K clip is about 220 MB, so about a minute per clip)
findings.note: Augustus, 2026-04-03, stated as Wi-Fi 6 on the 2.4 GHz band; a reply by Nagumich (2026-04-07) quotes the header as 5 GHz and says the A810S is 2.4 GHz only. The figure equals rcg530's front data rate (3.66 MB/s), so re-check the post before printing it.

findings.label: Frame rate and bitrate with front + rear recording together
findings.value: Front 4K at 24 fps, 29.4 Mb/s (HEVC, HDR); rear 1080p at 25 fps, 10.1 Mb/s
findings.source_title: 70mai 4K A810 Lite unboxing and first impressions by Augustus (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Augustus, 2026-05-23 and 2026-05-29. He states single-channel recording reaches 30 fps. The 24/25 fps cap is already on knowledgelib.io (crediting GameRevolution) and on DashCamTalk's roundup. Augustus names the front sensor as GalaxyCore GC8613, not a Sony STARVIS 2; that is his stated identification, not a teardown.

findings.label: Power draw
findings.source_title: 70mai 4K A810 Lite unboxing and first impressions by Augustus (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Augustus, 2026-05-22. The text I read does not say whether the rear camera was connected or how it was metered.

findings.label: Surface temperature after about 30 minutes in direct sun, 4K 24 fps two-channel, cool day
findings.value: microSD slot side 53.8 °C, underside vents 50.2 °C, port side 47.3 °C, LCD 39.3 °C; did not shut down
findings.source_title: 70mai 4K A810 Lite unboxing and first impressions by Augustus (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: Augustus, tested 2026-05-28, firmware 1.1.35ww. Cabin 11.5 °C, outside 14.3 °C, dashboard 24.6 °C. Ambient was about 21 °C cooler than his A810S test, so the two heat results are not comparable.

findings.label: Wi-Fi file transfer speed to phone
findings.value: 22.2 MB/s on the 5 GHz band (a one-minute 4K clip is about 222 MB, so about 10 seconds per clip)
findings.source_title: 70mai 4K A810 Lite unboxing and first impressions by Augustus (DashCamTalk forum)

findings.label: Power draw while driving, front + rear, and recorded bitrate
findings.value: 8.7 W; 24 + 24 Mbps (rear file 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, 23.8 Mb/s); rear camera alone about 3.8 W
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: TonyM, 2025-06-24 (8.7 W, 24 + 24 Mbps); EricSan re-measured 8.7 W the same day and gave the rear file bitrate on 2025-06-26. This is the 4K + 4K kit, which the brief lists at $239.99, over budget. Vantrue's S1 Pro Max 4K + 2.5K ($199.99 in the brief) and the S1 Pro 2CH ChatGPT named were not measured in this thread. Context only: 8.7 W is 41% more than the A229 Plus's 6.16 W with three cameras.

findings.label: Supply voltage at the bundled USB-A car adapter under load
findings.value: Sags from 5.18 V unloaded to 4.77 V; camera kept running
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum)
findings.note: EricSan, 2025-06-24 and 2025-06-25. Over-budget variant; context only.

findings.label: Typical parked current draw of a front + rear dash cam with motion detection and Wi-Fi
findings.value: About 0.25 to 0.45 A, against a typical 45 Ah car battery
findings.source_title: Best dash cams 2025: Reviews and buying advice (PCWorld)
findings.note: PCWorld's general figure, not a per-model measurement; this page is one ChatGPT cited. The A229 Plus's measured 0.453 A in 3-channel low-bitrate parking sits at the top of that range.

unsourced: DDPAI N5 Pro (our row): any measured bitrate, power draw, surface temperature or Wi-Fi speed. The DashCamTalk thread by lufa6977 (2026-09-13) and the Digital Reviews Network review by Lis Petersen (2026-09-08) carry only maker specs; a GadgetGuy review exists but I did not open it.
DDPAI Z50 Pro Dual and Botslab G980H 4K + 2K Dual: a named-reviewer measurement of any kind; one search found none for the Z50 Pro, and I did not search for the Botslab.

VIOFO A229 Plus in the 2-channel front + rear kit: watts while recording and in each parking mode, and Mbps per camera. rcg530's tables are images; a search snippet gave 4.27 W for 2CH front + interior in low-bitrate parking, but I could not open a page showing it in text, so it is left out.
VIOFO A229 Plus surface temperature with ambient stated (only the relative '16 °C cooler than the A229 Pro' was readable).
